ledger.note: 1104: Toghtekin takes Damascus on Duqaq's death and founds the Burid line. 'Following Duqaq's death in 1104, he seized the city for himself' (Burid page); the Toghtekin page: he had Tutush II proclaimed emir, married Duqaq's widow and took the title of atabeg, and held Homs from 1103 for Duqaq.

ledger.counterpart: holder not named by the page
ledger.note: 1110: Toghtekin captures Baalbek in April. 'In April 1110, Toghtekin besieged and captured Baalbek', installing his son Buri as governor.
1122: the Fatimids sell Tyre to Toghtekin ('The Fatimids sold Tyre to him'). Tyre had placed itself under his protection in 1111-1112.
1124: the Franks capture Tyre on 7 July ('the Franks captured it on July 7, 1124'). The kingdom-of-jerusalem and fatimid-caliphate dossiers record Tyre as passing from the Fatimids in 1124.

ledger.note: 1130: Zengi seizes Hama. He allied with Buri against the Crusaders, 'this was only a ruse to extend his power', and 'seized Hama from him'; Buri's son was taken prisoner.
1138: Homs goes to Zengi as a dowry. In May 1138 Zengi married Zumurrud Khatun 'and received Homs as her dowry'; Mu'in al-Din Unur had defended Homs in 1137.

ledger.note: 1139: Baalbek surrenders to Zengi on a promise of safe passage which 'he did not honor'; the territory was given to Najm al-Din Ayyub.

ledger.note: 1154: Nur ad-Din takes Damascus. He overthrew Mujir ad-Din 'with help from the population of the city' and 'Damascus was annexed to Zengid territory', unifying Syria 'from Edessa in the north to the Hauran in the south'; Abaq received fiefs near Homs. The page gives no month.

ledger.note: 1154: the Burid line ends with the capture of Damascus by Nur ad-Din (infobox: ended 1154, succeeded by the Zengid dynasty).

wars.name: Battle of Hab
belligerents: Crusaders (the Toghtekin page names no commander)
wars.outcome: Toghtekin was defeated at the Battle of Hab on 14 August 1119 after joining Ilghazi's campaign; no change of holder for Damascus.

wars.name: Battle of Azaz
belligerents: Crusaders (the Toghtekin page names no commander)
wars.outcome: Toghtekin and al-Bursuqi were defeated on 11 June 1125; Baldwin II's invasion of January 1126 was repelled and a late-1126 invasion of Antioch with Bursuqi achieved nothing. The Burid page adds a loss to the Crusaders at Marj al-Saffar in 1126.

wars.outcome: Zengi seized Hama (1130), besieged Damascus in 1135 without success, received Homs as a dowry (May 1138), took Baalbek (1139) and besieged Damascus again in 1139-1140; Damascus allied with Jerusalem against him.

wars.name: Siege of Damascus (Second Crusade)
wars.outcome: The Burids prevented the Second Crusade from taking Damascus; 'the crusader siege collapsed after only four days' (Nur ad-Din page).

notes:
A state Cliopatria lacks (cliopatria_names []). Four pages opened. Wikidata id not obtainable: null. The Burid page is thin (it names only Damascus); Toghtekin, Zengi and Nur ad-Din supply the territorial dates.
Not settled: when the Burids took Hama (confidence 1 at 1128); Banias and the Hauran (not on any page opened: the Burid page does not mention Salkhad or Banias; the Toghtekin page has no Banias, Hauran or Jabal Awf); Tyre: the kingdom-of-jerusalem dossier takes Tyre from the Fatimids in 1124, but the Toghtekin page has the Fatimids selling Tyre to Toghtekin in 1122 and the Franks taking it from him on 7 July 1124 (the Jerusalem dossier should name burid-dynasty as counterpart); Mujir ad-Din's relation to Nur ad-Din before 1154 (the Burid page says only that the dynasty ruled 'as subjects of the Seljuk Empire'); relations with the Assassins (not on the Burid page). The 'seljuks-of-syria' predecessor is a dossier written in this batch.
The mirrors in the zengid-dynasty dossier (1130, 1138, 1139, 1154) use the counterpart 'burid-dynasty' and the same Hama and Baalbek circles.
Gazetteer names used: Hama and Baalbek as coordinates (no place), others resolve.
